title: Durable Streaming (T-56987678)
description: Observability for SSE stream lifecycle, APNs silent push delivery, and event_index gap detection. Every panel maps 1:1 to a metric emitted by src/observability/streaming.rs. If a panel goes blank, the emission site in handlers/chat_stream.rs, handlers/conversation_worker.rs, or apns/silent_fanout.rs regressed — NOT the dashboard.

panels.title: Streams opened (cold vs resume)
panels.description: stream_opened_total split by the `resume` label. A cold-start is an SSE open without a `starting_after` cursor; a resume is an open with one. Used to tune retention + validate resume logic.

panels.title: Concurrent SSE streams
panels.description: stream_concurrent gauge — current number of open SSE streams. Each `record_stream_opened` increments by 1; each `record_stream_closed` decrements by 1. If this drifts below 0 or grows unbounded, a close path is missing. The integration test asserts a zero delta after balanced open/close.

panels.title: Stream closes by reason
panels.description: stream_closed_total labeled by DisconnectReason::Display. normal = worker signaled terminal event; client_disconnect = TCP/HTTP dropped; server_idle_timeout = no events for idle window; keepalive_timeout = ping failed; cursor_expired = 410 Gone; error = unhandled failure. Adding a variant to DisconnectReason requires updating this legend.

panels.title: Stream duration p50 / p95 / p99 (by reason)
panels.description: stream_duration_ms histogram quantiles. Short durations grouped by client_disconnect indicate churn (app backgrounded). Long durations grouped by normal are healthy active sessions. server_idle_timeout tail tells you the idle window is too tight.

panels.title: Events emitted per second
panels.description: stream_events_emitted_total — every event pushed to a live or replay SSE stream. Counts per-event, not per-stream. Rate gives events/s flowing through the pipeline.

panels.title: Bytes emitted per second
panels.description: stream_bytes_emitted_total — serialized JSON payload bytes shipped to clients. Divide by stream_events_emitted_total for mean event size.

panels.title: Resume vs cold-start ratio
panels.description: stream_resume_ratio gauge = resume_total / (resume_total + cold_start_total). Higher is healthier — means clients are reconnecting with a cursor rather than dropping the history. Near 0 means clients never carry state (check persistence on iOS). Computed inline on every record_stream_opened call.

panels.title: Cursor-expired 410 rate
panels.description: stream_cursor_expired_410_total — clients with `starting_after` older than oldest_retained. High rate means retention window is too short OR clients have been offline longer than the retention period (they should cold-start instead). Watch after any retention-window shrinkage.

panels.title: Event-index gap detection
panels.description: events_gap_detected_total — the event_index allocator returned a non-contiguous value. `gap_size = actual - expected` is added per detection. A gap means either (a) concurrent writers raced the allocator, or (b) a worker crashed mid-insert. Zero in steady-state is the health invariant.

panels.title: APNs silent push by result and status
panels.description: push_sent_total labeled by PushResult::Display (success/unregistered/bad_token/throttled/error) and apns_status (200/410/429/…). 410 is expected churn — it soft-deletes unregistered tokens. 429 is backpressure from APNs; the apns-collapse-id ensures the latest wake still lands. Split by both labels so operators can distinguish throttling (429) from unregistered (410) from 500-class errors without cross-referencing another panel.

panels.title: APNs push success ratio
panels.description: Fraction of silent-push attempts that returned HTTP 200. Dips below 0.95 indicate APNs sadness, token churn, or a regression in the fanout path. Excludes unregistered/bad_token (expected soft-deletes).

panels.title: Client session_start by platform
panels.description: clients_session_start_total labeled by platform + client_version. Emitted on every POST /api/device-tokens/register — once per iOS cold launch or token refresh. On a single-device deployment this is effectively launch-count.

panels.title: Stream rate-limit denials
panels.description: stream_rate_limited_total labeled by DenyReason::as_wire_str (concurrent_stream_limit | reconnect_rate_limit). One increment per 429 Too Many Requests response from the per-(user, conversation) SSE rate limiter (T-C410DD96). A sustained non-zero rate on reconnect_rate_limit usually means a client is in a reconnect loop; a sustained rate on concurrent_stream_limit means a single client opened more than one live stream.

panels.title: SSE keepalive frames sent
panels.description: stream_keepalive_sent_total — `ping` frames emitted by the SSE keepalive wrapper (T-CFFAF032). Expected cadence is ~1 frame every 15 seconds per active stream. A sustained rate near zero while stream_concurrent > 0 indicates the keepalive task stopped ticking — clients will idle-disconnect next.

panels.title: Retention — rows deleted per sweep
panels.description: retention_rows_deleted_total — throughput of the nightly retention prune (T-65DA4D32). Rate gives deletions/s during sweep windows; near-zero between sweeps is expected. A flat zero over 24h means the scheduler stopped firing.

panels.title: Retention — prune duration p95 / conversations touched
panels.description: retention_prune_duration_ms p95 (ms) and retention_conversations_touched (count per sweep). p95 duration climbing past the sweep interval is the first sign of prune lag. conversations_touched spiking unexpectedly may indicate a retention-window misconfiguration.

panels.title: Retention — earliest remaining event age
panels.description: retention_earliest_remaining_event_age_seconds — the age (seconds) of the oldest surviving conversation_event across the fleet. Load-bearing for the resume-token 410 Gone contract: if this climbs past the retention window, clients holding older cursors will cold-start when they should have resumed. Red threshold = retention_window + 1h buffer.
